title: Rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis and methotrexate
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's arthritis and related long-term drug therapy.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for rheumatoid arthritis.

HPI
The patient is a 77-year-old female who presents today for a scheduled follow-up regarding her chronic rheumatoid arthritis. She reports that her symptoms have been relatively stable over the past several months. She notes that while she still experiences some morning stiffness, it typically resolves within an hour of rising. She denies any new areas of swelling, significant increases in pain, or recent episodes of fever. She continues to take methotrexate on a weekly basis as prescribed and reports good adherence to her medication regimen. She also takes a daily folic acid supplement to mitigate side effects. She reports that her overall functional status remains good and she is able to perform most activities of daily living independently.

Medication List
- Methotrexate (weekly)
- Folic acid (daily)

Review of Systems
The patient denies chest pain, shortness of breath, cough, or fever. She denies any recent changes in vision or hearing. She denies unintended weight loss or night sweats. She reports no new skin rashes or rashes. She denies any changes in bowel or bladder habits.

Social History
The patient lives in a single-story home with her spouse. She retired five years ago and enjoys gardening and walking. She denies tobacco use and reports occasional social drinking.

Family History
Her mother had hypertension and her father had type 2 diabetes. She has one sibling with high cholesterol.

Vitals
Temperature: 98.6 F
Blood Pressure: 128/82 mmHg
Heart Rate: 74 bpm
Respiratory Rate: 16 breaths/min
SpO2: 98% on room air
Height: 5'4"
Weight: 145 lbs

Recent Labs
Hemoglobin: 12.4 g/dL
White Blood Cell Count: 7.2 x 10^3/uL
Platelet Count: 210 x 10^3/uL
Creatinine: 0.9 mg/dL
eGFR: 78 mL/min/1.73m2
ALT: 24 U/L
AST: 22 U/L

Exam
The patient is a well-appearing, alert, and oriented 77-year-old female in no acute distress. Her skin is warm and dry. Her gait is steady and she is able to bear weight symmetrically. No visible erythema or edema is noted in the extremities. Pulses are palpable and symmetric in all four limbs.

Assessment
1. Rheumatoid arthritis: The patient's condition is currently stable on her current maintenance therapy.

Plan
1. Continue methotrexate weekly.
2. Continue daily folic acid.
3. Follow up in three months for repeat laboratory monitoring and clinical assessment.

Electronically signed, E. Castillo, DO, 05/14/2026
explanations: Rheumatoid arthritis, nothing more specified: M06.9 (HCC 93).

distractors.why: Rheumatoid factor status is not documented.
Methotrexate has its own long-term use code, Z79.631.
